analysis:
The changes are CI-only: no provider runtime, coordinator contract, key handling, attestation or prefix-cache code changed, so I identified no regression against T-041 or the provider threats.

1) register-model.yml (lines 95-96) and release-desktop.yml (lines 59, 519) move jobs from blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404 to GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04. register-model adds timeout-minutes: 30. The job that holds MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY and the desktop publish job (contents: write) no longer run on a third-party runner. The coordinator URL allowlist (register-model.yml lines 101-111) still runs before the key-reading step (line 219 onward). No new secret exposure.

2) provider-tests.yml head 1052-1539 (visible part): the .git cache restore guard (symlink, hook, config denylist, fsck) at 1080-1105 and 1260-1285 appears unchanged. It is a denylist that does not cover other executing config such as filter.*, core.sshCommand or credential.helper. The poisoning prerequisite is a cache write, and saves are limited to SAVE_CACHES pushes. That is pre-existing and not attributable to this diff.

The changed lines are the tested-tree records (1514, 1517-1521, 1529, 1531-1539): a second tree-record artifact is uploaded with overwrite:true after full success. The provider-test-gate (1439-1492) still requires every non-skipped lane to succeed. Build jobs now run only when the lane is selected, and the plan selects none when skip is true.

Open integration questions, outside the supplied evidence: how scripts/ci-tested-tree.py and provider-plan.yml authenticate and look up these records, and whether a record can be forged or reused across trees or components. Whether test-cluster-gpu (new cluster_gpu input, lines 916-923, truncated) is enforced by the gate is also unverified. These concern CI integrity, not the runtime threat model.
